items.followUp: Define zero error and zero correction for a measuring instrument.

rubric.why: Defines zero error in terms of the instrument's reading when the true value is zero.
rubric.description: Zero error is the instrument reading when the true value is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an instrument shows a non-zero reading when the true value is zero, or equivalent wording.

rubric.why: Defines zero correction as the correction applied to remove zero error.
rubric.description: Zero correction is equal and opposite to zero error and is added to the observed reading.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that zero correction is equal and opposite to zero error, or that it is added to the observed reading to obtain the correct reading.

modelAnswer: Zero error is the reading shown by a measuring instrument when the true value is zero.
Zero correction is equal and opposite to the zero error; it is added to the observed reading to obtain the correct reading.

items.followUp: Define translatory motion and rotatory motion, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Identifies that the body's parts move together in translatory motion.
rubric.description: Translatory motion: all parts of a body move the same distance in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of translatory motion.

rubric.why: Identifies rotation about an axis as rotatory motion.
rubric.description: Rotatory motion: a body turns about a fixed axis, with its parts moving in circles around the axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of rotatory motion.

modelAnswer: In translatory motion, all parts of a body move the same distance in the same direction.
In rotatory motion, a body turns about a fixed axis and its parts move in circles around that axis.

items.followUp: Define force and write its formula in terms of mass and acceleration.

rubric.why: Gives the textbook meaning of force as a push or pull that changes or tends to change motion.
rubric.description: Force is a push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion of a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of force.

rubric.why: States Newton's second-law formula for force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing F = ma.

modelAnswer: Force is a push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or motion of a body.

items.followUp: Define momentum and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Identifies momentum as the product of mass and velocity.
rubric.description: Momentum is the product of a body's mass and velocity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition or formula p = mv.

rubric.why: Gives the SI unit of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct SI unit.

modelAnswer: Momentum is the product of a body's mass and velocity: p = mv.
Its SI unit is kg m s⁻¹.

items.followUp: Explain the difference between like and unlike parallel forces.

rubric.why: Distinguishes like parallel forces by their common direction.
rubric.description: Like parallel forces act in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that like parallel forces act in the same direction.

rubric.why: Distinguishes unlike parallel forces by their opposite directions.
rubric.description: Unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.

modelAnswer: Like parallel forces act in the same direction.
Unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.

items.followUp: Define gravitational field strength and write its formula and SI unit.

rubric.why: States that gravitational field strength is gravitational force per unit mass.
rubric.description: Gravitational field strength is the gravitational force acting per unit mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying force per unit mass.

rubric.why: Locates the definition in the field and/or states the defining relation.
rubric.description: It is the force per unit mass at a point in a gravitational field; g = F/m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying the field point or giving g = F/m. The SI unit N/kg is also acceptable supporting detail.

modelAnswer: Gravitational field strength is the gravitational force acting per unit mass at a point in a gravitational field.
g = F/m; its SI unit is N/kg.

items.followUp: Define energy and name the two types of mechanical energy.

rubric.why: Gives the standard definition of energy.
rubric.description: Energy is the capacity to do work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining energy as the capacity or ability to do work.

rubric.why: Names both types of mechanical energy.
rubric.description: The types of mechanical energy are kinetic energy and potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both kinetic and potential energy.

modelAnswer: Energy is the capacity to do work.
The two types of mechanical energy are kinetic energy and potential energy.

items.followUp: A 20 kg body is raised 5 m. Calculate its potential energy, taking g = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: Identifies the given quantities with their SI units.
rubric.description: Given: m = 50 kg, h = 4 m, g = 10 m s⁻².
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly listing the given mass, height and gravitational acceleration.
Award 1 mark for writing the correct formula.

rubric.why: Substitutes the given values into the formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution, with units shown.

rubric.why: Gives the correctly calculated potential energy with a unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 50 kg, h = 4 m, g = 10 m s⁻².
Substitution: PE = 50 kg × 10 m s⁻² × 4 m.
